paragraphs: Teacher Kim has two big pictures on the board. "Look at them before break," she says. "They show two places in our country." The pictures are new, and they are very big. Sam and May look at the first picture. "What's this?" asks May. "It's a tall building," says Sam. "What's that?" asks May. "It's a bus, and that's a big road," says Sam. "It's the city!" they say.

Ben looks at the second picture. "What's this?" he asks. "It's a green field," says May. "And what's this?" asks Ben. "It's a tractor on a farm," says Sam. "I can see a river too." There are cows in the field. The river is long and blue. "It's the countryside," says Teacher Kim. "The two places are very different."

"How are they different?" she asks. "The city has a lot of buildings," says May. "The countryside has fields," says Ben. "The city is busy and loud," says Sam. "The countryside is quiet," says May. "Good!" says Teacher Kim. "Your homework is a picture of your place." "Draw it, and write: This is ..." Sam smiles. "I live in the city, but my grandpa has a farm!"
text.summary: Teacher Kim shows two big pictures, one of the city and one of the countryside. The children ask "What's this?" and find out how the places are different.
